stem: A grieving family describes cultural practices they would like to follow after a client's death. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.A: Ask about the family's preferences and incorporate their cultural practices into care when they can be safely accommodated
options.B: Use the same mourning expectations for every family so care remains standardized
options.C: Discourage cultural rituals because grief should be expressed privately outside the health care setting
options.D: Use the nurse's own beliefs to determine which mourning practices are appropriate

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes incorporating the client's cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care and providing end-of-life care and education. Therefore the nurse should assess the family's preferences and respectfully incorporate their practices when safe and feasible. B, C, and D impose standardized or nurse-centered expectations rather than individualized culturally responsive care.
educational_objective: Provide culturally responsive grief and end-of-life care by assessing client/family preferences and incorporating their cultural practices and beliefs when safely feasible.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14: incorporate client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care; provide end-of-life care and education to clients
source_claim_supported: Entry-level RN psychosocial care includes incorporating client cultural practices and beliefs into care and providing end-of-life care and education.

blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14

correction_summary: Replaced the vague secondary-source claim that grief expression 'varies significantly across cultures' with the directly testable NCSBN requirement to incorporate each client's cultural practices and beliefs. Removed the colleague narrative, made the response client/family-specific, and retained the safety/feasibility condition rather than promising universal accommodation. Difficulty adjusted from hard to easy.
audit_findings: A directly implements the NCSBN activity statement. B, C, and D substitute standardized or nurse-centered values for individualized cultural assessment. The item avoids stereotyping any culture or prescribing a specific mourning ritual. One best answer remains with no second answer, cueing, unsupported cultural generalization, or unresolved conflict.
